cultivar: Fuxuan 9, Fuding Dabai, Wuniuzao, Pingyang Tezao
processing: A flat green tea: the leaf is heated to stop oxidation, pressed straight and flat, then dried until smooth; the finished tea is noted for a chestnut aroma.
harvest_season: Very early spring is the selling point, as the name 'extra early' says; exact dates vary by year and are not fixed in the appellation record.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight and smooth leaves of even length, yellow-green to emerald with faint down.
taste_profile: Fresh and clean with a rich, lasting chestnut aroma and a brisk, savoury-sweet finish.

brewing.notes: Tender early leaf can turn bitter fast, so keep to about 80°C and lift the lid after pouring.

vintage_note: Sold fresh as the current year's very early spring tea, which is the whole appeal of the name, and best drunk within about a year. Grade and picking date matter more than the region name, since the appellation spans 12 towns.
description:
Naxi Tezao is an early spring green from Naxi District in Luzhou, close to where the Yongning River joins the Yangtze. The name simply means extra early, and being first to market is the idea behind it.

It is made in the flat, straight style, smooth and even, from improved cultivars brought into the district such as Fuxuan 9, Fuding Dabai, Wuniuzao and Pingyang Tezao. So this is a modern industry built around variety choice, rather than an old local plant.

The cup is bright yellow-green, with a rich chestnut aroma and a fresh, clean finish. Water around 80°C works well for the tender grades; anything hotter tends to flatten the aroma.

The protected zone covers 12 towns and 176 villages, so expect a range of quality. Check for the picking date and grade, and do not assume early means better for every lot: the earliest tea is prized for freshness, not always for depth.
history:
Tea is a modern pillar industry in Naxi: by 2011 the district reported about 150,000 mu of gardens, some 4188 tonnes of tea, and 40 processing companies, after a push to introduce early-budding cultivars.

It was registered as an agricultural geographical indication on 20 December 2011, then included in the first group of protected names under the China-EU geographical indication agreement, on a list dated 20 July 2020.
